summary.headline: The Advisory Committee voted to recommend a $73.46 million FY27 budget, excluding $820,000 for Atwood site cleanup, and supported 22 Town Meeting warrant articles.
summary.summary: The Southborough Advisory Committee recommended an FY27 town budget of $73,455,973 after removing $820,000 for the Atwood site remediation to allow for further review of project scope and requirements. The committee approved a $75,000 Reserve Fund transfer to replace a condemned facilities utility van. Members also reviewed 36 draft articles for the upcoming Annual Town Meeting, voting to recommend approval on 22 articles including capital bonding, road maintenance, and a proposal to change the Town Clerk from an elected to an appointed position.

topics.title: FY27 operating and capital budget review and vote
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the latest FY27 budget model, which stood at a 4.64 percent year-over-year expenditure increase with a $553,000 levy balance. Key adjustments included shifting a $75,000 fire brush truck to the Ambulance Fund, deferring a $262,425 DPW dump truck lease to next year, and modeling employee transitions to high-deductible health plans. The committee debated school technology bonding and voted 3-2 to keep the $365,000 school technology capital bond before voting 5-0 to recommend the overall town budget of $73,455,973, which removed $820,000 for Atwood site remediation pending confirmation of DEP requirements.
key_details: Recommended total FY27 expenditures of $73,455,973, representing an estimated 4.64 percent increase over FY26.
Removed $820,000 for Atwood site remediation from the spring warrant, deferring action to fall unless DEP rules require immediate bonding.
Voted 3-2 to support a $365,000 capital bond for school technology infrastructure and classroom equipment.
Deferred a $262,425 DPW dump truck to next fiscal year to reduce expenditure totals.
The town anticipates long-term annual savings of up to $750,000 if municipal employees migrate toward high-deductible health plans.
topics.outcome: Recommended FY27 budget total of $73,455,973 by a 5-0 vote, excluding the $820,000 Atwood site remediation article.
topics.why_it_matters: Determines the municipal and school spending plan presented to voters at Annual Town Meeting on April 11, directly affecting residential property tax rates.

topics.title: Reserve Fund transfer for facilities utility van
topics.summary: The committee considered a request from the town administrator for a $75,000 transfer from the Reserve Fund to replace a facilities utility van. The 2018 vehicle was recently condemned by town mechanics due to severe rot and structural issues on its undercarriage. Using the Reserve Fund enables the town to order a replacement immediately rather than waiting for FY27 capital appropriations.
key_details: Transfer amount: $75,000 to the Facilities Equipment account.
The 2018 utility van was taken out of service due to structural undercarriage failure.
The department had been paying rental fees while operating out of rented vehicles.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved meeting minutes from October 20, 2025 and December 8, 2025 with one typographical correction.
key_details: Minutes of October 20, 2025 and December 8, 2025 approved 5-0.

topics.title: Town Meeting warrant articles review and recommendations
topics.summary: Members examined the 36 articles drafted for the April 11, 2026 Annual Town Meeting warrant to determine which items to recommend, put on consent, or hold for further testimony. The committee voted to recommend a consent batch of 19 articles covering recurring appropriations, capital bonds, and bylaws. It also voted to recommend Article 15 (Trottier school roof replacement bond), Article 16 (special legislation petition for a Costco liquor license), Article 26 (changing Town Clerk to an appointed role), and Article 29 (delinquent tax payment agreements).
key_details: Voted 5-0 to recommend consent batch articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, and 27.
Voted 5-0 to recommend Article 15 for the Trottier Middle School roof replacement project and Article 16 for a Costco liquor license.
Voted 5-0 to recommend Article 26 to transition the Town Clerk position from elected to appointed by the Select Board.
Voted 5-0 to recommend Article 29 authorizing the treasurer-collector to enter into delinquent tax installment agreements.
Held planning and zoning articles 17 and 31 through 34, Article 28 regarding Willow Street easements, and citizen petitions 35 and 36 for future meetings or Town Meeting.
topics.outcome: Recommended approval of 22 warrant articles across several motions and held remaining articles for further review.
topics.why_it_matters: The committee's recommendations guide voters at Annual Town Meeting on bonding, zoning changes, and town operational governance.

topics.title: Upcoming meeting schedule and logistics
topics.summary: The committee scheduled upcoming meetings to draft the Advisory Committee letter to voters and review remaining held warrant articles with town boards. Members noted the Planning Board's public hearings on zoning articles on March 23 and agreed to meet next on March 25, with an additional tentative meeting set for March 30.
key_details: Next regular meeting scheduled for Wednesday, March 25, 2026 at 7:30 PM.
Planning Board public hearing on zoning articles noted for Monday, March 23, 2026 at 6:30 PM.
Tentative meeting scheduled for Monday, March 30, 2026 at 7:00 PM if needed.
topics.outcome: Set meeting dates for March 25 and March 30.

votes.motion: Approve Reserve Fund transfer of $75,000 to the Facilities Equipment account for a replacement utility van.
Support the FY27 capital bond for school technology infrastructure and equipment in the amount of $365,000.
Recommend to Town Meeting the FY27 operating budget and capital expenditures totaling $73,455,973, excluding the $820,000 Atwood site remediation capital bond.
Support warrant articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, and 27 as printed in the draft warrant.
Support warrant Article 15 (Trottier roof replacement) and Article 16 (Costco liquor license petition).
Support warrant Article 26 to change the Town Clerk position from elected to appointed.
Support warrant Article 29 to authorize treasurer tax installment payment agreements.

public_comment.summary: A resident and School Committee member commented on the $365,000 school technology item, stating that it funds new interactive smart boards across all classrooms that currently lack them rather than routine replacements of older technology.
A resident and town official reminded the committee that the Planning Board would hold public hearings on all zoning warrant articles at its meeting on March 23.

upcoming.what: Planning Board public hearings on zoning warrant articles
Advisory Committee meeting to review remaining articles and draft voter letter
